source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Recognizing and responding to potential complications, including the ability to rescue a client from a deeper-than-intended level of sedation","B":"Fairly minimal formal training of any kind, since moderate sedation is generally considered a fairly low-risk procedure for a nurse to monitor","C":"The independent ability to administer general anesthesia without any additional physician involvement or oversight","D":"Mainly the ability to record basic vital signs at set intervals throughout the sedation procedure itself"}}
source_row.rationale: Nurses monitoring moderate sedation must have specific training in recognizing and responding to potential complications, including the ability to rescue a client if sedation becomes deeper than intended, per facility and regulatory standards.
source_row.source_detail: Required Nursing Competency for Sedation Monitoring
